title: Jude and the Summer
premise: Marine biologist Freya Eastwick has spent eleven years on a Cornish island counting turtles and avoiding love, ever since Jude Ashcombe vanished the summer they were nineteen. When a storm-damaged post office finally delivers a letter he wrote her in 2014 — a confession she never received — she learns he never chose to leave; his family forced him out after an accident that ruined another islander. Now Jude returns to sell his late grandmother's cottage and face the town's quiet verdict, and Freya must decide whether the truth absolves him or whether justice belongs to the people he hurt. As the last ferry of the season approaches, Freya uncovers evidence that clears Jude's name, but clearing it means exposing her own uncle's role in the cover-up. In the end, Jude stays past the last train and misses the last ferry deliberately, choosing Freya and the island over the clean escape he once took.
about_author: Zephyrine Nakamura is a former tide-pool census volunteer who writes love stories set where the land runs out of road. She lives between two coastal towns and insists every novel must contain at least one missed departure.

chapters.title: The Post Office That Forgot
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. A storm floods the island's shuttered post office, and the postmaster hands Freya a water-stained letter addressed to her, postmarked eleven years ago. She recognizes the handwriting before she reads the name. Emotional beat: dread wrapped in curiosity — the past knocking with wet knuckles.

chapters.title: Turtle Season
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. She buries the letter unopened in her field kit and throws herself into tagging loggerhead hatchlings with her colleague Priya. The routine of counting keeps her steady. Emotional beat: controlled avoidance; we learn she measures everything except her own heart.

chapters.title: What the Letter Said
chapters.summary: Freya's POV, night. Alone with whiskey and rain, she opens it: Jude writes that he is being sent away, that the accident at Harrow Point wasn't what people think, and that he'll come back for her when it's safe. He never did. Emotional beat: grief reopened like a healed wound split by salt.

chapters.title: The Ferry Brings a Ghost
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude Ashcombe steps off the early ferry with a suitcase and his grandmother's death certificate, intending to clear the cottage and leave within a week. He sees Freya on the dock and forgets how to breathe. Emotional beat: hope colliding with guilt.

chapters.title: Eleven Years of Weather
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Their first conversation is all small talk stretched thin over deep water — turtles, tides, the price of paint. Neither mentions the letter. Emotional beat: two people fluent in avoidance, speaking carefully around the thing itself.

chapters.title: Harrow Point
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. He visits the cliff where, at seventeen, a boating accident injured old Tam Pengelly; the town decided Jude's family's money bought silence. Flashback reveals his father shipped him away within days. Emotional beat: the weight of a story told about you until you half believe it.

chapters.title: The Cottage Full of Grandmother
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya helps Jude sort his grandmother Edith's belongings and finds Edith's diary hinting she knew the truth about Harrow Point — and kept receipts, literally, in a tin box. Emotional beat: intimacy rebuilt through shared archaeology of a house.

chapters.title: Almost
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A power outage strands them together; almost-kiss interrupted by Priya arriving with news that Tam Pengelly's health is failing. Jude withdraws, convinced he has no right to want anything here. Emotional beat: longing punished by conscience.

chapters.title: Tam Pengelly
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya visits Tam, who is sharp-tongued and unrepentant: whatever happened, the town needed someone to blame and the rich boy fit. But his eyes flicker when she mentions Edith's name. Emotional beat: the discovery that victims can also be keepers of convenient lies.

chapters.title: The Tin Box
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. They open Edith's tin: insurance documents, a repaired winch receipt dated before the accident, and a note suggesting the boat's rigging was sabotaged — not neglected. Someone else was on the water that night. Emotional beat: vertigo; the ground truth shifts under them.

chapters.title: Who Else Knew
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya cross-references the harbor logbook and finds pages missing from the week of the accident — pages her uncle Alastair, then harbormaster, would have signed off. She tells herself there's an innocent explanation. Emotional beat: loyalty beginning to crack against evidence.

chapters.title: Rising Water
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Word spreads that Jude is back asking questions; islanders grow cold, someone keys his rental car, and Freya is warned at the pub to stop digging. They grow closer precisely because the world pushes. Emotional beat: us-against-the-island intimacy.

chapters.title: Alastair's Version
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Her uncle admits he removed the logbook pages — but claims he did it to protect Tam, who was drunk at the helm that night and begged him to. The sabotage theory, he says, is Edith's grief inventing villains. Emotional beat: a plausible lie that fits too neatly.

chapters.title: The Middle Distance
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Doubting everything, Jude nearly takes the midweek ferry out. At the dock he turns back, finds Freya waiting in the rain without knowing why she came. First kiss, finally. Emotional beat: choosing to stay before knowing if staying is right.

chapters.title: Edith's Last Summer
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. In the diary's final entries, Edith describes seeing lights on the water the night of the accident — a second boat, unregistered, belonging to a family friend of the Pengellys. Tam wasn't drunk; he was covering for his own nephew. Emotional beat: the truth assembling itself like a skeleton recovered from sand.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Harbor
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Freya and Jude confront Tam's nephew, Callum, now a respected fisherman, with the diary and the winch receipt. He breaks: the rigging was cut to void an insurance claim gone wrong, and Tam took the blame's shape to protect blood. Emotional beat: justice surfacing, ugly and human.

chapters.title: What Justice Costs
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Going public means exposing Alastair's falsified logs and Tam's complicity — destroying reputations, maybe prosecutions. Freya realizes clearing Jude requires burning down people she loves. Emotional beat: the theme made flesh — justice outside the law has no free version.

chapters.title: The Last Train
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude's solicitor urges him to sign the cottage sale and leave before the fallout; the last mainland train connection leaves Saturday morning. He packs. Freya finds the empty hooks where his coat hung. Emotional beat: the old pattern threatening to repeat — departure as reflex.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. At a packed harbor meeting, Freya presents the evidence herself, naming Alastair and shielding nothing, including her own family's shame. The room splits; some apologize to Jude, some turn on her. Emotional beat: her loneliest and most honest moment — identity claimed at cost.

chapters.title: Climax: The Last Ferry of the Season
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Sunday evening, the final ferry departs until spring. Jude stands at the dock with his ticket as the crowd watches, everyone certain he'll go. He lets it leave without him, then walks through the gathering dark to find Freya on the beach among emerging hatchlings. Emotional beat: the whole book's image fulfilled — staying as the truest confession.

chapters.title: After the Season
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Weeks later: Alastair faces inquiry, Tam and Jude reach a fragile peace over tea, and the cottage comes off the market. Freya and Jude begin again slowly, without the past tense. Emotional beat: quiet repair; love as something maintained, not rescued.

chapters.title: Epilogue: Next Summer
chapters.summary: Shared POV, brief alternating sections. One year on, the first ferry of the new season arrives carrying tourists, and neither of them is on it — they're on the headland counting turtle nests together, a letter framed above Edith's old mantel. Emotional beat: inheritance reclaimed; the summer that finally got to be theirs.
